# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 70/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16 ÷ 23 × 100 = 70. High = (16 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 70.

The site is mostly set up well: crawlers are allowed in, the navigation uses real links, and policy matches robots.txt. The losses come from a few small, fixable gaps. Nothing is unknown, because everything that decides these rules is in the repository. This score comes from reading the code. I did not check a running site.

## Live check

**Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Point crawlers at your sitemap
- **Why it matters:** The sitemap exists, but robots.txt doesn't mention it. Crawlers that read robots.txt first won't be told where it is.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1-5`
- **What the code says:** the file has only `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` and a `GPTBot` block, with no `Sitemap:` line.
- **Size:** Small. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`.
- **Score after this:** 18 ÷ 23 = **78**

### 2. Set the page language on `<html>`
- **Why it matters:** `lang` tells browsers, screen readers and machines which language the pages are in. Every page is missing it.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small. Change it to `<html lang="en">`, which matches `site.language` in your config.
- **Score after this:** 18 ÷ 23 = **78**

### 3. Add canonical URLs to /docs and /blog
- **Why it matters:** A canonical is the one official address of a page. It stops duplicate addresses from competing. Only the home page and /pricing set one.
- **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };`
- **Size:** Small. Add `alternates: { canonical: 'https://www.ledger.example/docs' }`. For /blog, add the canonical in a server `layout.tsx` or `page.tsx` for that route, because `app/blog/page.tsx` is a client component and can't export metadata.
- **Score after this:** 17 ÷ 23 = **74**. Also removing the noindex on /pricing, if it is unintended, brings it to 17.25 ÷ 23 = **75**.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |

| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. 3 of 4 routes clear |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on indexable URL | Problem | Only `/` is clear (1 of 4). `/docs` and `/blog` have none. `/pricing` points its canonical at a noindex page |
| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | `app/blog/page.tsx:8` has `fetch('/api/posts')` in `useEffect`. 3 of 4 routes clear |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap valid and discoverable | Problem | `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line. Site-wide |

| GEO-016 | Key routes linked in server HTML | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:13`, plain `<a href>` to all four pages |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits vs AI-search policy | Clear | Only a scoped `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:15`. No page-wide nosnippet |

## Other problems found

- **A noindex page is in your sitemap and navigation.** `public/sitemap.xml:4` lists `https://www.ledger.example/pricing`, and `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` sets `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. The page also sets a canonical to itself. The signals contradict each other. Remove the noindex if people should find pricing, or remove it from the sitemap if not.

## Worth considering

- **Blog posts with their own pages:** `app/blog/page.tsx:10`: `posts.map((p) => <article key={p.id}>{p.title}</article>)`. Render the list on the server and give each post its own address, so the posts exist as text and links.
- **Pricing that delivers what it promises:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` describes "Plans for every team size", but the page says only `Free for up to three people.` Listing the actual plans and prices as text would answer the obvious question.
- **Thin docs page:** `app/docs/page.tsx:4`: `Start by importing your bank feed.` One sentence is all the setup guide has. Real steps would give readers something to quote.
- **Product and organization labels:** nothing states the site's identity in a machine-readable way. Organization or WebSite JSON-LD with the name "Ledger" and `https://www.ledger.example` could be added in `app/layout.tsx`.
- **Distinct blog title and description:** `app/layout.tsx:5-6`: `title: 'Ledger: accounting for small teams'`. /blog has no metadata of its own, so it shares the home page's title and description.
- **Dates in the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-6` has no `<lastmod>`. Add dates for pages that change, such as the blog.
- **Generated sitemap:** the sitemap is hand-kept. `app/sitemap.ts` would keep it in step with the routes.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Blog content:** `/api/posts` isn't in this repository, so I can't see what the data contains. A live check would show what the blog serves to crawlers.
- **Live status codes and headers:** whether the server returns 200 for each page, and any `X-Robots-Tag` headers set outside this repository.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools and search engines to find this site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.
- I treated `/thank-you` as deliberately noindex and left it out of the route counts. It isn't in the sitemap or the navigation.
- I read `geo.config.json`, `package.json`, the layout, all 5 pages, `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`. That is every file in the repository.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
